scale_note: Nominal block width approximately 4 mm. Epidermal thickness, appendages, vessel calibres, receptors and cellular details are selectively exaggerated; counts are representatives, not densities. Visible cutaways and hidden-tissue gaps are pedagogical dissections. Neither route colors nor sequence steps encode physiological time, measured fluid concentrations, tissue optics or receptive-field size.

native_contract.animation_status: Manual caption/camera/visibility/selection progression only. No morph animation, simulated secretion, moving particles, stimulus deformation, muscle contraction or electrophysiology.
native_contract.variant_contract: Configure machine variant_id pre_refine or post_refine separately before ProceduralModel, with verified native-cache SHA-256 and display label Pre refine or Post refine. Restore and discard a live session before switching. All required selectors must resolve exactly for delivered variants. Explicit legacy_mode=True is metadata compatibility only, never delivery-ready.
native_contract.render_state_opacity: Per-view alpha_multipliers are transient state.part_alpha, restored with session; no saved material or mesh mutation.

variant_policy.compatibility: Missing final detail is rejected by default; no silent substring matching, omitted anatomy or identical Before/After fabrication.

views.purpose: Locate four epidermal strata, the dermis, follicles, glands and deep sensory context in a generic hairy-skin block.
Compare basal, spinous, granular and cornified cell organization while retaining the dermoepidermal boundary.
Expose dendritic melanocytes with a basal keratinocyte neighborhood; removed overlying layers are a teaching dissection.
Locate the anagen bulb, dermal papilla, sheaths, sebaceous unit and arrector attachments.
Inspect the cellular matrix cupping a mesenchymal papilla and the transition toward keratinized hair.
Keep shaft and both sheaths present together so their distinct radial and axial relationships remain visible.
Show the inner-sheath termination, sebaceous junction, upper follicular canal and surface exit.
Inspect peripheral basal cells, differentiating lipid-filled sebocytes and the outgoing duct as separate compartments.
Trace an explicitly schematic static route from a holocrine acinus through its duct and upper follicle to the skin surface.
Relate the smooth-muscle band to the follicular bulge and superficial connective-tissue anchorage.
Keep the secretory coil, outgoing dermal duct and epidermal course together; this unit opens independently of the follicle.
Expose secretory-cell profiles, peripheral myoepithelium and an explicitly schematic lumen-content representative.
Distinguish two-layered cuboidal duct cells from the secretory coil while following the same luminal route.
Compare the eccrine surface pore with the separate follicular route for hair and sebum.
Relate deep arterial supply, superficial exchange and venous return to epidermis and appendage beds.
Place free endings, follicular endings and a deep lamellar receptor with their represented tissue targets.
Hide the surrounding lamellae as a dissection step while retaining the entering axon and tissue anchorage.
Distinguish a lobule-level tissue representative, magnified cellular contents and the connective septa.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Differentiating epidermal keratinocytes renew a cornified barrier.

steps.caption: Basal keratinocytes renew the epidermis. Their attachment to the underlying basement-membrane region differs from cell-to-cell desmosomal contacts.
Spinous cells maintain keratin filaments and desmosomal contacts as differentiating cells become flatter toward the surface.
Granular cells contain keratohyalin granules. Separate lamellar organelles deliver extracellular barrier material; these two structures must not be conflated.
Flattened, anucleate corneocytes and extracellular lipids form the surface barrier. Shedding and renewal continue; this thin-skin model has no stratum lucidum.

schematic_limitations: Manual stages describe differentiation, not tracked cells, mitosis, permeability or timed turnover.
No universal four-week renewal clock is assigned; histological profiles and displayed counts are representative.
Lamellar secretion and tight-junction barrier maturation overlap. No lipid bilayer, lamellar-body fusion or tight-junction simulation is supplied.
Hidden strata create dissection gaps, not epidermolysis, tissue loss or physiological separation.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Basal melanocytes distribute pigment to neighboring keratinocytes.

steps.caption: A basal melanocyte extends dendrites between neighboring keratinocytes; the epidermal melanin unit is a cellular relationship, not a population count inferred from this block.

Pigment reaches neighboring keratinocytes from melanocyte dendritic processes. Human-skin and coculture experiments support melanocore exocytosis followed by keratinocyte uptake; this is a mechanism supported by those experiments.
Pigment can collect above keratinocyte nuclei, contributing to UV protection. The neighborhood is a magnified teaching representative; no UV dose or protection level is computed.

schematic_limitations: The static dendrites and neighborhood do not implement vesicle transport, membrane fusion, pigment synthesis or measured transfer.
The specific transfer mechanism is evidence-qualified rather than asserted as an exclusive universal pathway.
The selector Melanocyte dendrite tips identifies cell processes, not resolved melanosomes.
Hair-bulb melanocytes are not inferred from the epidermal Melanocytes selector; hair pigment is explained by caption only.

functional_sequences.mechanism: An anagen follicle produces keratinized hair and an inner root sheath around a mesenchymal dermal papilla.

steps.caption: This represents a growing, anagen follicle. The shaft, inner sheath, outer sheath, matrix and dermal papilla are different compartments of one pilosebaceous unit.
Proliferating matrix epithelium cups the vascular connective-tissue papilla. The papilla supports growth signaling and supply; it does not turn into hair.
Matrix descendants differentiate upward into the hair shaft and inner root sheath. The keratinization transition marks a tissue stage, not a simulated moving front.
The inner root sheath guides the growing shaft. The outer root sheath is continuous with epidermal epithelium and remains a distinct outer compartment.

The inner root sheath ends below the represented sebaceous outlet, in the source isthmus–infundibulum-junction vicinity. The upper canal carries hair and sebum to the surface; fine body hair need not contain a medulla.

schematic_limitations: No follicular cycle, stem-cell lineage, elongation, keratinization kinetics or shaft displacement is simulated.
Primary dermal-papilla ablation evidence was obtained in live mice; it supports a signaling role, not human timing or the specific source geometry.
Visible cell detail is representative. Inner-sheath sublayers are not separately selectable unless explicitly added by the final source recipe.
Removing a sheath is dissection, not a normal hair-growth stage. Papilla and matrix must remain separately identifiable in the native cutaway.

The source IRS endpoint remains at 0.70 L; the outlet is at min(0.70 L + 0.085 L, ORS upper bound), not exactly 0.70 L. Both positions are authored representative landmarks in the isthmus–infundibulum-junction vicinity, not measured biological ratios. The connective sheath has a marked teaching truncation and contact windows; it is not an uninterrupted capsule.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Sebocytes differentiate and disintegrate, supplying sebum to a short duct and follicular canal.

steps.caption: Peripheral basal sebocytes provide a renewing cell population for each sebaceous acinus.
Sebocytes mature inward and accumulate lipid. Near the outgoing duct, terminally differentiating cells disintegrate and contribute their contents to sebum: holocrine secretion.

The short sebaceous duct enters the upper follicle above the represented inner-sheath endpoint, in the source isthmus–infundibulum-junction vicinity. The static sebum route is an overlay; native passage continuity still requires validation.
Sebum reaches hair and adjacent skin through the follicular canal. The neighboring eccrine duct has its own surface opening and carries sweat.

schematic_limitations: No living cell is destroyed by the viewer and no lipid flux is computed.
Holocrine secretion is not apical pinching or simple exocytosis. Mouse DNase2-deletion experiments support a distinct terminal cell-death mechanism, explained only by caption.
A colored route is not a patent duct, fluid, simulated flow or a duct-connectivity proof.
Native validation must confirm acinus-to-duct and duct-to-follicle continuity without creating an opening directly through the skin beside the follicle.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Smooth-muscle contraction transmits force between follicular and dermal attachments.

steps.caption: The arrector pili joins the follicular bulge region to superficial dermal connective tissue. Smooth-muscle cell nuclei distinguish this tissue from a generic strap.
Contraction pulls against dermal anchorage and changes the follicular angle, producing piloerection and a surface goose bump. Human scalp histology shows splaying fibers within upper-dermal collagen.
The muscle passes beside the sebaceous unit and may assist movement of already produced sebum. Contraction does not create sebum or replace sebocyte differentiation.

schematic_limitations: Only camera, visibility, focus and caption change. No muscle shortening, follicular rotation, mechanical contact force or goose-bump deformation is implemented.
The model does not calculate thermoregulatory benefit or imply that piloerection is a major cooling route in humans.
The attachment study concerns human scalp. Broad attachment principles inform this representative body-skin unit without claiming matching regional microanatomy.

functional_sequences.mechanism: A deep secretory compartment produces sweat; a distinct duct reabsorbs salt and delivers it independently to the skin surface.

steps.caption: Follow one eccrine unit from its deep secretory coil to the outgoing dermal duct and coiled epidermal passage. This route is separate from the hair follicle.
Secretory clear-cell and dark-cell representatives surround the gland lumen; surrounding capillaries supply the gland. The blue content representative indicates a lumen, not measured sweat.
Sympathetic cholinergic stimulation activates secretion. Peripheral myoepithelial cells are contractile; isolated human-gland imaging supports a contribution to sweat transport.
The duct has basal and luminal cuboidal cell layers. Its luminal transport machinery, including ENaC and CFTR, reabsorbs salt from the sweat.
Ductal salt absorption makes ordinary surface sweat more dilute than the primary secretion. The amount varies with conditions; this model does not calculate concentration.
The eccrine epidermal passage opens on the skin surface rather than draining into the follicle. Sweat evaporation can remove heat; the visible route does not calculate cooling.

schematic_limitations: The secretory portion and duct differ by cell organization and function, not just blue color.
No channel mesh, salt ion particles, concentration gradient, lumen-pressure model, peristaltic animation or secretion-rate simulation is supplied.
Ex vivo cholinergic myoepithelial contraction evidence does not define a universal in-vivo wave speed or require uniform contraction of the entire gland.
The lumen-content selector is explicitly schematic and is hidden outside relevant route views.

The native deep coiled region can include both secretory and coiled ductal segments. This source partitions a representative secretory coil from an ascending duct; secretion must not be inferred from deep location or coiling alone.
Do not describe a selected static duct as a clinically normal sweat test or diagnose channel disease from it.
Eccrine stromal fibers are sparse connective-tissue context samples; they are not a gland capsule or another duct wall.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Vessels support dermal and appendage tissue and supply the avascular epidermis by diffusion.

steps.caption: Deep cutaneous branches supply the dermis and appendage beds. The follicular-sebaceous and eccrine capillary representatives associate circulation with the tissues it serves.
The superficial network gives rise to papillary capillary loops. Oxygen and nutrients cross into interstitial tissue and reach the avascular epidermis by diffusion; no vessel enters its strata.
Venous channels collect blood from the exchange networks. Loose papillary connective tissue and coarser irregular reticular collagen provide different supporting contexts.

schematic_limitations: Vessel courses are schematic representatives, not a resolved hemodynamic model or literal blood colors.
No oxygen concentration field, red-cell transit, endothelial permeability or vasomotor animation is computed.
Display arrows, if later added, must stop diffusion explanation at tissue exchange and must never portray an epidermal blood vessel.
Legitimate capillary–tissue proximity and appendage supply contacts are retained; hiding dermis creates a dissection space.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Different peripheral endings sample hair movement, superficial stimuli and deep vibration.

steps.caption: Deflection of a hair can stimulate endings around its follicle. Human hairy-skin recordings identify rapidly adapting hair units; a visible ring is a representative arrangement, not one receptor per hair.
Free endings approach or enter the living epidermis and represent pathways for pain, temperature and itch. Their generic geometry does not identify every sensory subtype.
A deep Pacinian representative places a terminal within concentric lamellae. Its envelope shapes dynamic mechanical input; the model does not calculate adaptation or a preferred vibration frequency.
Hiding the lamellae exposes the entering axon and central terminal. The central terminal is a receptor component, not a vessel or fluid drain.

schematic_limitations: No hair bending, skin indentation, afferent conduction, stimulus threshold, firing-rate trace or receptive-field calculation is implemented.
Hairy skin has additional afferent types beyond this subset; no claim of complete innervation is made.
Meissner corpuscles are not part of this new generic hairy-skin specimen. The preserved original cache may contain them; it must not silently supply the delivered function contract.
Cited Meissner distribution research examined particular human glabrous regions; it does not establish sparse Meissner occupancy in all hairy body skin.
Rapid adaptation and receptor specificity are captions, not animated spikes or electrophysiology.

Human scalp microscopy identifies lanceolate axon–terminal Schwann cell complexes outside the outer root sheath near the isthmus/upper bulge. This does not establish that every follicular ending has one adaptation class, nor universal body-vellus density; terminal Schwann-cell microanatomy is not separately resolved by the final selector recipe.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Adipose cellular organization and fibrous septa support, cushion and connect the skin block.

steps.caption: The retained Adipocytes (fat lobules) host is a lobule-level tissue representative. New cellular markers show a magnified cell membrane, lipid droplet and peripheral nucleus within that tissue.
Fibrous septa separate and connect adipose lobules and carry larger vessels and nerves. These partitions are connective tissue, not empty molds left when fat is removed.

schematic_limitations: No triglyceride metabolism, adipocyte-volume change, tissue mechanics or insulating performance is simulated.
Representative cellular details do not convert a lobule into one giant adipocyte. The historical host selector is preserved for exact integration while its description must clarify scale.
Source layer positions and enlarged appendages are pedagogical; counts are not specimen densities.

review.camera_status: Source-landmark poses only; framing and tissue occlusion have not been visually accepted.

deferred_checks: Native framing for every named function view, including rear-context pigment neighborhoods and foreground matrix/duct routes.
Guarantee all 61 exact selectors independently for newly built Pre refine and Post refine caches; Meissner corpuscles must be absent from the new generic hairy specimen.
Confirm matrix cups papilla with a distinct basement-membrane region and neither structure disappears in the longitudinal diagnostic section.
Confirm sebaceous duct enters a patent follicular canal; static route overlay is not accepted as a substitute.
Confirm eccrine secretory lumen joins duct lumen and the acrosyringium reaches a surface pore that is distinct from the follicular ostium.
Opaque, reverse and isolated-host inspection of cell detail, sheath changes, muscle attachments and appendage capillary relationships.
No blood vessels within epidermis; free sensory endings may cross its boundary.
Validate saved descriptions clarify cellular vs lobular representatives and anatomical vs cutaway openings.
Native roundtrip of function state with custom opacity, clipping, isolate, peel, explode and reveal state; no variant arrays or files may change.
Every selected variant retains independent provenance and output validation. Source-only schema checks cannot establish native/anatomical acceptance.
